To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maize histone deacetylease Hda1 is expressed as an inactive protein that is processed to a smaller, active enzyme form by limited proteolysis and that the enzymatically inactive full-length form of ZmHDA1 is not active as a repressor in reporter gene assays.

maize histone deactylase Hda1 is expressed in all germinating tissues and is synthesized as an inactive 84-kilodalton (kD) protein that is proteolytically processed to an enzymatically active 48-kDa protein form by limited proteolysis.
maize Hda1 is a protein that is synthesized as an inactive precursor protein of 84 kD, which is processed to an active protein of 48 kD by a proteolytic mechanism that involves a 65-kd intermediate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation and function of the Rpd3/HDA1-type histone acetylases in maize.
the regulation of maize histone deacetlyase Hda1 and how the regulation of this enzyme may affect the regulation of gene expression in the maize plant.
the identification and characterization of the histone deacetylation system of maize, which has been shown to be involved in transcriptional regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ZmHDA1 is an RPD3/HDA1 homolog in maize and that the enzymatically inactive 300-kD complex and the 84-kD form represent a novel regulatory mechanism for the RPD3/Hda1 family.
the 48 kDa form of ZmHDA1 is enzymatically active as a histonedecetylase and is the form that is involved in the repression of the reporter gene.
HDA1 encodes a histone deacetlyase that is expressed in all maize tissues and that is regulated by proteolysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the maize histone deactylase Hda1 and have shown that the protein is processed to an enzymatically active form in a proteolytic cleaveage step.
the 48 kDa form of Hda1 is active as an enzyme and repressor, whereas the 84 kDa form is inactive.
the maize histone deacetlyase is processed by a regulated proteolysis to an active form.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-terminal part of ZmHDA1 is not required for histone deacetylation activity but is essential to repress transcription.
the C-terminal part of Hda1 is not essential for its enzymatic activity, but it is important for the full repression activity of Hda1 in a reporter gene system.

the processing of the histone deacety-lase HDA1 in maize embryos is regulated during germination in vivo, which is in line with our previous findings that HDA1 is involved in regulating the expression of the major storage proteins in maize.
